name: Williams Hill
summary: Pope County, IL summit lookout: 60-ft steel Forest Service tower c.1942; Easter service notices 1948 and 1955; 1958 column; 1972 sale notice; now marked gone.
status_note: FFLA Illinois list marks it gone; the sources read give no removal date and do not describe the summit now

events.note: Described as Williams Hill Lookout Station, U.S. Forest Service, 60-foot steel tower, altitude 1,065 feet, two miles due west of Herod (description dated c.1942)

Notice of March 22, 1948 (The Daily Register) announced the third annual Easter sunrise service, sponsored by the American Sunday School Union, would move to the Williams Hill tower from the High Knob Tower in Hardin County, where it had been held for the past two years

Notice of March 30, 1955 (The Daily Register) announced the annual outdoor Easter service at the Williams Hill tower at 3 p.m. on Easter Sunday, April 10; the sources read do not confirm that it was held

Column of July 3, 1958 (The Daily Independent): the two buildings had been moved away; the tower was not manned by the Forest Service in summer; the little building at the top was kept locked; climbing the tower was possible; picnic grove with three tables
Southern Illinoisan notice of 18 August 1972 asking for bids on the sale of this and seven other steel lookout towers on the Shawnee National Forest
